newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila T-bill market focus on short-term bills.
newsitem.headline: Manila T-bill market focus on short-term bills.

text.p: Trading activity was focused on the 35-and 42-day T-bills on Wednesday after they fetched attractive rates at the auction, traders said.
"They crowded out the longer-tenor bills from three months to one year," a foreign bank dealer said.
Banks are buying short-term bills and selling those with longer maturities, traders said.
The 35-day rate averaged at 17.558 percent at the auction on Tuesday, and the 42-day averaged at 17.283 percent.

However, "we might see aggressive selling of these bills tomorrow," the trader said, citing that it was expensive to hold on to these bills with the central bank still borrowing overnight at 25 percent.
Meanwhile, banks started to raise their bid and offer quotes for the one-year bills after the rates on these bills slid at Monday's auction.
"This is a technical correction. We believe the fall was overdone," a trader said.
The average interbank call loan rate was steady at 25.0625 percent, with 28 lenders and 13 borrowers. Volume was higher at 14.16 billion pesos from 12.38 billion.
